Well, for one, the tuning of an instrument often fluctuates subtly from one note to another. One note may be a few cents flat, and other notes a few cents sharp. Sometimes this is done intentionally to compensate for the problems of equal temperament, and sometimes this happens unintentionally due to poor instrument quality. A good example of this can be found on most guitars: tune an open string to a tuner, and then play this string on the first fret and you'll commonly find that the first fret in substantially sharp. In other words, it's common for musicians to fluctuate several hertz. In fact, if that didn't occur the notes would sound like a square-wave, like a robot sound: not very beautiful.

Secondly, I've heard people mention that 432 hertz is the resonance node of the human body. This is silly. Everyone's body is a different size and therefore would resonate to a different pitch.

If there is anything remotely conspiratorial regarding musical tuning, it would be temperament. The 20th century created equal temperament, a tuning system that proceeded well-temperament, and pythagorean temperament before that. The result is that everything is now slightly out of tune, in order for musicians to modulate into distantly related keys, and pantonal (atonal) playing.
